summary: The final rule introduces a distinction between senior executives and other workers regarding the enforceability of existing non-compete clauses, which was not present in the proposed rule. It also modifies definitions, such as 'non-compete clause,' and removes the definition of 'employer' while adding a separate definition for 'person.' The final rule incorporates public comments and provides model language for notice requirements to workers affected by the rule.

key_changes.topic: Scope of Ban on Non-Compete Clauses
key_changes.proposed: The proposed rule provided a comprehensive ban on non-compete clauses, declaring it an unfair method of competition for employers to enter into, maintain, or represent the enforceability of non-compete clauses with workers. (Proposed Rule, § 910.1)
key_changes.final: The final rule bans new non-compete clauses for all workers but allows existing non-compete clauses for senior executives to remain enforceable, while existing non-competes for other workers are no longer enforceable after the effective date. (Final Rule, Summary)
key_changes.change_description: The final rule introduces a distinction between senior executives and other workers regarding the enforceability of existing non-compete clauses.

key_changes.proposed: The proposed rule did not explicitly address notice requirements for workers affected by the unenforceability of existing non-compete clauses. (Proposed Rule, § 910.1)
key_changes.final: The final rule requires employers to provide notice to workers with existing non-compete clauses that these clauses are no longer enforceable, and includes model language to facilitate compliance. (Final Rule, Summary)
key_changes.change_description: The final rule adds a notice requirement for workers affected by the unenforceability of existing non-compete clauses.

key_changes.proposed: The proposed rule defined 'employer' as 'a person, as defined in 15 U.S.C. 57b-1(a)(6), that hires or contracts with a worker to work for the person.' (Proposed Rule, § 910.1)
key_changes.final: The final rule does not adopt a definition of 'employer' but instead uses the term 'person' throughout the regulatory text. (Final Rule, § 910.1)
key_changes.change_description: The final rule removes the definition of 'employer' and adopts a separate definition for 'person.'

key_changes.proposed: The proposed rule defined 'non-compete clause' as a contractual term preventing a worker from seeking or accepting employment or operating a business after the conclusion of employment. (Proposed Rule, § 910.1)
key_changes.final: The final rule modifies the definition to include terms or conditions of employment that penalize or effectively prevent a worker from seeking or accepting work or operating a business, whether written or oral. (Final Rule, § 910.1)
key_changes.change_description: The final rule expands the definition of 'non-compete clause' to include workplace policies and oral agreements that function as non-competes.

unchanged_elements: The Commission's reliance on Section 5 of the FTC Act as the legal basis for the rule remained consistent. (Proposed Rule, § 910.1; Final Rule, § 910.1)
The rule's focus on post-employment restraints, rather than concurrent-employment restraints, remained unchanged. (Proposed Rule, § 910.1; Final Rule, § 910.1)

definitions.proposed_definition: A partnership, corporation, association, limited liability company, or other legal entity, or a division or subsidiary thereof. (Proposed Rule, § 910.1)
definitions.final_definition: A partnership, corporation, association, limited liability company, or other legal entity, or a division or subsidiary thereof. (Final Rule, § 910.1)

definitions.proposed_definition: Work for an employer, as the term employer is defined in § 910.1(c). (Proposed Rule, § 910.1)
A person, as defined in 15 U.S.C. 57b-1(a)(6), that hires or contracts with a worker to work for the person. (Proposed Rule, § 910.1)
A contractual term preventing a worker from seeking or accepting employment or operating a business after the conclusion of employment. (Proposed Rule, § 910.1)
definitions.final_definition: A term or condition of employment that prohibits, penalizes, or effectively prevents a worker from seeking or accepting work or operating a business after the conclusion of employment, whether written or oral. (Final Rule, § 910.1)

definitions.proposed_definition: Not explicitly defined; referenced in the definition of 'employer' as defined in 15 U.S.C. 57b-1(a)(6). (Proposed Rule, § 910.1)
definitions.final_definition: Any natural person, partnership, corporation, association, or other legal entity within the Commission's jurisdiction, including any person acting under color or authority of State law. (Final Rule, § 910.1)
